title: an any-erased capability argument and a const value alias for the capability class both name the same capability, so Layer.succeed registers it and Layer.provide still subtracts it
notes: specification/requirements.mdx, 'Layer Algebra': 'A layer MUST associate each capability's nominal context key with a compatible service instance. Layer APIs are library-shaped; the compiler recognizes their effect on R without introducing special provider grammar.' and 'Satisfaction': 'Providing a layer to a computation MUST remove matching capabilities from the computation's unsatisfied requirement row.' An `<any>` assertion and an `as any` are TYPE-only: they are erased before anything runs, and the value `Layer.succeed` receives is the same `Directory` class object it would have received without them. `const Store = Directory` is not a wrapper at all but a value binding whose initializer IS the class, so the object reaching the registry is again `Directory`. In all five spellings the nominal key the runtime holds is `Directory`, so the subtraction must happen and the program must run. WHY THIS CASE EXISTS: `SMITHERS2106`'s settled rule — resolve a capability reference by SYNTAX first and by TYPE second, and refuse what cannot be pinned to exactly one class declaration — governs the `X.context()` receiver and was found on 2026-08-27 not to be applied at `Layer.succeed`'s FIRST argument, one argument away from a site the corpus already covered. The two implementations were wrong in OPPOSITE directions there, which is why an accepting case is the one that catches both. The Go fork refused all four erasing spellings — `SMITHERS2104` at 30:19, 31:19, 33:19 and 34:19 — because an `any` operand pins no class in the type. The reference did not refuse: it published a PHANTOM row. `rowNameOfClassReference` fell back to the identifier's own text, so `Layer.succeed(Store, directory)` recorded a capability literally named `Store`, the `Directory` the body requires was never subtracted, and `main` came out carrying `requirements ["Directory"]` for a program whose layer provides exactly that. A fail-open and an over-refusal on the same five lines, and no case in a 498-case corpus reporting `0 divergent` touched any of them. WHY IT IS `expect: "output"` AND NOT `"diagnostics"`: the reference's half of the defect was visible only in a requirement ROW, and no corpus expectation can read a row — nor could it be compared across backends if it could, because the Go protocol carries no rows at all. The observable form of the same statement is that a single `Layer.succeed(Directory, directory)` subtracts every one of these and the program runs to completion. WHY THE OUTPUT IS NOT FIVE IDENTICAL LINES: two of the five look up 'zoe' rather than 'ada' and one is stamped by a SECOND capability, so the printed lines are `Ada`, `none` and `Ada@7` in a fixed order. A resolver that quietly reordered, dropped or duplicated a provide scope would produce a permutation, and a permutation of five identical lines is invisible. The `Layer.merge` entry is the only one whose output depends on a second capability actually reaching the body. WHAT IT ADDS OVER ITS SIBLING: `a-layer-through-a-type-only-wrapper-is-the-same-layer` already holds two capability-argument spellings, a parenthesis and a `satisfies` — both of which PRESERVE the type. Every spelling here either ERASES the type (`<any>`, `as any`) or reaches the class through a BINDING (`Store`), and those are precisely the two shapes on which a type-directed resolver and a syntax-directed one give different answers. A resolver that reads the checker's type passes every one of the eight accepting spellings in the sibling and fails four of the five here. WHAT THIS CASE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CONTAIN: a REASSIGNED binding. `let C = Directory; C = Twin; Layer.succeed(C, directory)` is accepted and panics at run time on BOTH backends today. That is not a hole this rule left — it is `SMITHERS2106`'s own pre-existing residual, and the identical shape at the `X.context()` receiver behaves the same way, untouched; closing it needs a new rule that has to move both walks together, and `const`-ness alone would over-refuse aliases that run. It is pinned as an explicit known-residual UNIT test (`poc/src/language/layer-capability-argument.test.ts`) and deliberately kept out of the corpus, because a corpus case over that shape could only encode today's acceptance as the contract — which is the opposite of what a case is for. `06-layers/a-mutable-layer-binding-is-opaque` is the reassigned binding at the LAYER position, where the answer IS settled and IS refusal; the capability argument does not have that answer yet. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the THIRD declared stdout line from `Ada` to `none` — the claim that the `const Store` alias does not reach the body, which is precisely the spelling the reference got wrong — turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, `["Ada","none","Ada","none","Ada@7"] != ["Ada","none","none","none","Ada@7"]` on each. The third line is chosen because the first two are the erasing casts, which the FORK got wrong, and the alias is the one the reference got wrong; a mutation on either alone would be satisfied by one of the two pre-fix behaviours. The expectation was restored byte-identically (sha256 397f07d52c32c11b638a9918cdfeee20744ef049d5b8a069413d50720f5df334 before and after, that digest being this file's content at the moment the mutation ran — this sentence is appended afterwards, so the shipped file necessarily hashes differently). The mutator refuses to run at all unless the case is green on BOTH backends first AND its search string occurs exactly once in the file; both refusals were exercised against this case rather than assumed, because a search string that matches nothing mutates nothing and comes back green.
